Subject: Addon pricing: retention + tracing + advanced dashboards

Hi Naomi —

Thanks again for the demo this week. We liked the visibility features; before procurement kicks off I need a firm picture of how addons will be packaged and priced so I can build the SOW and budget request. Quick context: Brightlane expects to run 30M inference requests/month initially, and our engineering team needs 90-day trace retention for incident investigations plus 30-50 advanced dashboard seats for product analytics.

Can you confirm:
- Pricing model options (metered vs slab/seat) for retention and tracing
- Example cost for our volumes on a 12-month commit vs pay-as-you-go
- Any promotional pilot credits or demo allowances we can include in the procurement package
- Standard SLOs and overage smoothing for spikes

Procurement would like pricing and a short SOW by Jun 30. We are hoping for a 20-30% concession off list on the first year if we commit. Is that something you can share quickly?

Best,
Alyssa Cheng
Head of Platform Programs
Brightlane

Subject: RE: Addon pricing: retention + tracing + advanced dashboards

Alyssa — thanks for the clear ask and the timeline. Looping in Ben (AE) and Kimberly (pricing lead) so we can give you options and a short SOW. Below are three pragmatic paths we commonly offer — I included rough monthly figures for the volumes you mentioned (30M requests/mo). I attached a short pricing matrix (retention_pricing_v2.pdf) and a draft pilot SOW (sow_pilot_draft.docx).

Option A — Metered (low commitment, simple):
- Tracing ingestion: $0.015 per trace-ingest unit (estimated 60k units/day =~ $27k/mo).
- Retention add-on: 90-day tiered storage: ~$4,200/mo (includes hot storage + 1x daily snapshot).
- Advanced dashboards: $120/seat/mo -> 40 seats = $4,800/mo.
- Total estimated: ~$36k/mo on PAYG. No annual commit discount; monthly overages billed.

Option B — Committed annual (recommended for cost predictability):
- 12-month commit reduces trace ingestion and retention unit price by 20% (example: trace => $0.012/unit, retention => $3,360/mo).
- Dashboards: seat bundle: 40 seats at $95/seat/mo = $3,800/mo.
- Estimated total: ~$28k/mo effective (20% lower than PAYG).

Option C — Hybrid + Pilot concession (best for enterprise procurement):
- 12-month commit with stepped discounts: 25% off list in year 1 if you commit to baseline: 25M requests/mo equivalent and retention baseline 90 days.
- Pilot: 3-month pilot with $5,000 credit toward addon consumption and one onboarding workshop included.
- Smoothing: monthly usage cap with 30% buffer before overage applies; overages prorated at the committed rate for the remainder of the term.

What we can offer (negotiation space):
- We can extend the pilot to 6 months and increase the one-time credit to $7,500 if you commit to a 12-month baseline within 30 days of pilot start.
- We can also consider a 25% first-year discount on addons for a straightforward 12-month financial commit; 30% is borderline but possible for larger committed spend or a multi-product enterprise agreement.

Next steps (suggested):
1) Confirm expected ingestion ranges for traces (avg/day peak/day) and number of active dashboard seats; we used proxy estimates above.
2) Ben will send a short commercial term sheet and the SOW; Kimberly will validate exact SKU pricing and finalize discount structure depending on commit level.
3) If acceptable, we’ll prepare a DocuSign-ready SOW and a pilot schedule.

I attached the pricing PDF and the draft SOW. Ben/Kim — anything to add on commercial guardrails?

Thanks,
Naomi Feldman
Head of Sales Operations, Redwood Inference
naomi_feldman@redwood.ai

2) They ask for a firm 30% first-year discount in the commercial term for the overall addon bucket to justify internal sign-off. We understand this may require a minimum committed baseline — our current best-case baseline would be 20M requests/mo and 30-day heavy trace retention to start.

If you can give us a written pilot offer (6 months, $7.5k-$10k credit, onboarding, and a 25-30% first-year discount with a 12-mo conversion right), we can move procurement to review and target a signature by Jul 8.

Alyssa — thanks, and totally reasonable asks. We want to make this easy for Brightlane and protect predictable economics for both sides. Summary of confirmed concession path: 

- Pilot: 6 months, $7,500 pilot credit applied to addon consumption only. Onboarding workshop and two health-check sessions included.
- Conversion: If Brightlane signs a 12-month paid commitment within 30 days after pilot end, we will provide 25% off list prices for addons in year 1.
- Stretch: A 30% discount is available if Brightlane commits to a higher baseline (>=30M requests/mo equivalent OR minimum $300k ARR committed across core + addons).
- Overage smoothing: first 3 months post-conversion — smoothing buffer of 40% for usage before overages apply; overages after that billed at committed rates.
- Caps: We will include a quarterly review clause. If sustained usage is >200% of committed baseline across 2 consecutive months, we reserve the right to renegotiate unit rates.

Next steps: Ben will drop the commercial term sheet into HubSpot (id: 123456) and I’ll attach a DocuSign SOW for the pilot (link: https://www.docusign.com/sign/ABCDEF-1234567890). Kimberly will finalize SKU language and provide a redlineable pricing appendix.

If that sounds good, Alyssa, can you confirm final baseline numbers (requests/day, expected average traces/day, dashboard seat counts) so we lock the SOW? Procurement timeline of Jul 8 is doable from our side once the term sheet is in place.

Thanks — looking forward to getting Brightlane into pilot.
